checklist.area: Ownership admission, force, cancellation and conditional handoff
checklist.evidence: Traced daemon ACP dispatch through Broker::prepare/commit and the existing control registry. Force remains authority-only; pending cancellation and conditional keep/withdraw retain their established semantics and admitted work.

checklist.area: Original native connection authority and physical input routing
checklist.evidence: Reviewed NativeControl worker routing, captured grants, application-input gates, warning/consent handling and original-connection checks in src/control.rs. ACP events are consumed without raw PTY fallback.

checklist.area: Compound claim liveness across pause and shutdown
checklist.evidence: src/tui/control.rs rechecks stop and heartbeat after claim observation and before ownership-claim. Connection::drop shuts down the owning socket. The controlling-PTY regression holds the actual compound observation and verifies no ownership mutation reaches the daemon.

checklist.area: Initial session establishment and strict target identity
checklist.evidence: Resume::validate permits only null-to-established session identity on the same daemon/view/instance/connection. The stale snapshot-to-inspect path refreshes observation without retrying a mutation; dedicated source regressions cover establishment both during disconnection and between snapshot and inspect.

Reviewed src/acp_profiles.rs and projects configuration integration: bounded closed defaults, existing configuration persistence, shell-free executable resolution, explicit unavailable-profile rejection and argv-free profile discovery.

checklist.area: Human CLI and native picker launch routing
checklist.evidence: Traced AcpStart through request_for, tui::start, NativeControl::launch, daemon acp-open and broker reservation/start. Optional CLI fields are removed by request_for; the native worker supplies its original controller. Picker requests use actual project IDs.

src/tui.rs exits on pause/socket loss before consuming a queued successful launch receipt, and also checks authority connectivity after poll but before take_launched. NativeControl::stop then clears the receipt. See E06-R2-01.

Reviewed settings validation, advertised-ID resolution, ordered original configuration RPCs, acknowledgement checks and mismatch/rejection handling. Prompt admission remains blocked until configuration reaches readiness; no fallback setter or unadvertised model is introduced.

Configuration projections distinguish requested/reported values and unreported defaults, and track later displacement. The native editor disclaims permission guarantees; the launch dialog documents inherited values and option merging.

checklist.area: OMP cancellation and opaque tool identities
checklist.evidence: Traced Configure RPC dispatch/results, configuration notifications, $/cancel_request and enlarged tool-call IDs through tool updates, elicitation and permission consumers. Cancellation uses the exact typed responder ID and cannot replace an already admitted winner.

checklist.area: Reconnect, stale state disposal and no implicit reacquisition
checklist.evidence: Outside the launch-receipt defect, recovery stops the old worker, constructs fresh native provenance, drains intercepted events, resets local editor/control state, disables auto-acquisition and connects only to the existing socket. Tests address each original transport independently.

Resume validation rejects changed daemon identity, known-session replacement, missing targets and ended original instances rather than selecting a same-name replacement. Recovery does not call ensure_daemon or launch another agent.

Reviewed new profile/settings limits against existing frame, interaction, RPC and process-lifecycle accounting; cancellation retains its original responder. Test cleanup retains explicit pre-fallback process/worker/termios/sentinel assertions, and the live driver avoids formatting private provider content.

Reviewed the frozen production/test paths and relevant README, changelog, conventions, manifests, scope, plan contracts and threat model. New tests drive actual client/daemon/PTY paths with observable effects. The launch-loss regression specifically cuts the receipt-following snapshot, leaving the earlier receipt-consumption window uncovered; that gap is included in E06-R2-01 rather than counted as another defect.

findings.title: Preserve acknowledged launch receipts before fencing a lost connection
findings.impact: A successfully launched live agent can be abandoned by the attachment even though the native worker has already parsed its successful acp-open reply. Picker recovery returns to the previous view; the default human CLI launch can instead recover its empty pre-launch target and display Ended, while the newly created agent remains running under the departed controller.
findings.evidence: The worker sends successful Op::Launch results through its reply channel (src/tui/control.rs:298-305), and received stores the exact target in self.launched (lines 620-626). However, attached returns on pause or either socket failure before polling that channel (src/tui.rs:1039-1049). There is a second loss window at lines 1068-1073: poll can consume the launch success and then a subsequent transport error/channel disconnection, but the connectivity return occurs before take_launched at line 1074. In both cases Resume still describes the old/empty active view, and authority.stop clears self.launched at src/tui/control.rs:374. The existing launch-loss regression deliberately cuts only the snapshot sent after the UI has consumed the receipt, so it does not exercise either ordering.
findings.fix: Persist successfully acknowledged launch identity independently of usable authority, including on the pause/connection-loss teardown path, before stop discards local replies. Drain or retain only the launch receipt for continuity; do not process/replay queued authority or repeat acp-open. Add a causal regression that lets the worker publish launch success, then loses either transport before the UI consumes it, and verifies recovery selects that exact newly launched instance once.

report.summary: Blind source review FAIL: one must-fix launch-continuity race remains. Thirteen of fourteen applicable control areas passed source inspection (92.86%); the failed area can lose a successful launch receipt during connection or pause fencing. No separate style, documentation-only or speculative findings are reported.
report.limits: Read-only E06 round-2 source review against base 2195b05 and the frozen manifest, including relevant existing consumers. No edits, builds, tests, linters, formatters, runtime/version probes, browser activity or provider calls were performed. The finding is established by source-level ordering, not a newly executed reproduction. Supplied runtime results were not rerun or treated as independent verification; complete real-OMP/live acceptance remains unproved and no additional live request was consumed. Historical E03/E04/E05 gates and caps are unchanged. No prior review reports, repair dispositions or self-audits were used.
